_instructions: Score every hint for the pair it sits under. 'already_served' is context only: do not score it.

hints.explanation: Nike sells Air shoes, and in Greek myth Nike is the goddess of victory.

lines.AIR: Nike Air shoes are known for their air-cushioned soles.
lines.VICTORY: In Greek myth, Nike is the goddess of victory.

hints.explanation: In Aesop's fable, the ant works all summer while the grasshopper plays.

lines.ANT: The ant stores food for winter in The Ant and the Grasshopper.
lines.WORK: The grasshopper plays instead of working in the fable.

hints.explanation: Crash Bandicoot is a video game hero, and bandicoots are small marsupials from Australia.

lines.AUSTRALIA: Bandicoots are marsupials native to Australia and New Guinea.
lines.CRASH: Crash Bandicoot is a classic PlayStation hero.

hints.explanation: A sack is a bag, and in football a sack is tackling the quarterback before he can throw.

lines.BAG: A sack is a large bag.
lines.FOOTBALL: A football sack is tackling the quarterback behind the line before he passes.

hints.explanation: Heavy metal icon Ozzy Osbourne famously bit the head off a bat on stage in 1982.

lines.BAT: Ozzy bit into a bat thrown on stage, reportedly thinking it was a toy.
lines.HEAVY: Ozzy rose to fame singing heavy metal with Black Sabbath.

hints.explanation: Oysters grow in oyster beds, and some oysters make pearls.

lines.BED: Oysters are farmed and found in oyster beds.

hints.explanation: Alfred Hitchcock made Psycho, with its shower scene, and The Birds.

lines.BIRD: Hitchcock's The Birds is about birds attacking a town.
lines.SHOWER: Hitchcock's Psycho has the famous shower scene.

hints.explanation: Plasma is the liquid part of blood and also a state of matter.

lines.BLOOD: Plasma is the yellowish liquid that carries blood cells.
lines.STATE: Plasma is a state of matter, alongside solid, liquid and gas.

hints.explanation: Jaws is a steel-toothed James Bond henchman, and also the shark in Spielberg's 1975 film.

lines.BOND: Jaws, the giant with steel teeth, fights Bond in two films.
lines.SHARK: Jaws is the classic film about a great white shark.

hints.explanation: Schrodinger's cat is a thought experiment about a cat sealed in a box.

lines.BOX: In the thought experiment, the cat is sealed in a box.
lines.CAT: In theory, Schrodinger's cat is both alive and dead until the box is opened.

hints.explanation: Bubble tea is also called boba, and Boba Fett is a Star Wars bounty hunter.

lines.BUBBLE: Bubble tea is often called boba tea.
lines.STAR WARS: Boba Fett is a famous Star Wars bounty hunter.

hints.explanation: Nicolas Cage starred in National Treasure.

lines.CAGE: Cage is the actor's stage surname; he was born Nicolas Coppola.
lines.TREASURE: Nicolas Cage plays the treasure hunter in National Treasure.

hints.explanation: Scarecrows guard cornfields, and candy corn is a Halloween treat.

lines.CANDY: Candy corn is a Halloween candy.
lines.SCARECROW: Scarecrows are a classic sight in cornfields.

hints.explanation: A mustang is a free-roaming wild horse, and the Ford Mustang is a classic car.

lines.CAR: The Ford Mustang is a classic American car.
lines.WILD: Mustangs are the free-roaming wild horses of the American West.

hints.explanation: A flute is a wind instrument and a tall champagne glass.

lines.CHAMPAGNE: Champagne is often served in a tall flute.
lines.WIND: The flute is a woodwind instrument.

hints.explanation: China's Terracotta Army is thousands of life-size clay soldiers buried with the first emperor.

lines.CHINA: The Terracotta Army was found in China in 1974.
lines.SOLDIER: Each terracotta figure is a clay soldier.

hints.explanation: To groom is to clean and tidy up, and the groom is the man getting married.

lines.CLEAN: Grooming means cleaning and tidying, as cats groom their fur.
lines.WEDDING: The groom is the man getting married at a wedding.

hints.explanation: Espresso is strong coffee served in shots.

lines.COFFEE: Espresso is a concentrated way of brewing coffee.
lines.SHOT: A single serving of espresso is called a shot.

hints.explanation: Cotton is spun into thread, and cotton candy is spun sugar.

lines.COTTON: Cotton fibers are spun into thread and yarn.
lines.SUGAR: Cotton candy is made by spinning melted sugar into threads.

hints.explanation: Jiminy Cricket sings "When You Wish Upon a Star" in Disney's Pinocchio.

lines.WISH: Jiminy sings "When You Wish Upon a Star".

hints.explanation: Pixar's Coco is about Mexico's Day of the Dead.

lines.DEAD: Coco centers on Día de los Muertos, the Day of the Dead.

hints.explanation: Die Hard is a classic action film, and die is the singular of dice.

lines.DICE: One of a pair of dice is called a die.
lines.HARD: Die Hard is the 1988 Bruce Willis action film.

hints.explanation: In Back to the Future, Doc Brown's dog Einstein rides alone in the DeLorean on its first time-travel test.

lines.DOG: Doc Brown's dog Einstein is sent one minute into the future in the DeLorean.
lines.EINSTEIN: Doc named the dog after Albert Einstein, the famous physicist.

hints.explanation: Daenerys Targaryen is called the Mother of Dragons.

lines.DRAGON: Daenerys hatches three dragons in Game of Thrones.
lines.MOTHER: Among her titles, Daenerys is called Mother of Dragons.

hints.explanation: Easter Island's moai are the giant stone figures known as Easter Island heads.

lines.EASTER: The moai stand on Easter Island in the Pacific.
lines.HEAD: The moai are nicknamed Easter Island heads, though many have bodies buried below.

hints.explanation: Sprite is a lemon-lime soda, and a sprite is a fairy.

lines.FAIRY: A sprite is a small fairy or spirit in folklore.
lines.LEMON: Sprite is a lemon-lime soft drink.

hints.explanation: Old MacDonald had a farm in the nursery song.

lines.FARM: Old MacDonald's farm is full of animal noises.
lines.OLD: The song is Old MacDonald Had a Farm.

hints.explanation: The decathlon is a contest of ten track and field events.

lines.FIELD: The decathlon includes field events like the shot put and javelin.
lines.TRACK: It also includes track races like the 100 meters and 1500 meters.

hints.explanation: A bass is a fish and also a deep-voiced instrument like the bass guitar.

lines.FISH: Largemouth bass are popular fish with anglers.
lines.INSTRUMENT: The bass guitar and double bass are instruments.

hints.explanation: In the song, an old lady swallows a fly and then a spider to catch it, and a swallow is a bird that catches flying insects.

lines.FLY: The old lady first swallows a fly, and swallow birds catch flies in midair.
lines.SPIDER: She swallows the spider to catch the fly.

hints.explanation: The Statue of Liberty holds a torch and was a gift from France.

lines.FRANCE: France gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States.
lines.TORCH: Lady Liberty holds up a torch.

hints.explanation: The Trojan Horse was a wooden horse that the Trojans took in as a gift, with Greek soldiers hidden inside.

lines.GIFT: The Trojans accepted the horse as a gift.
lines.HORSE: The Trojan Horse was a giant wooden horse.

hints.explanation: Homer was an ancient Greek poet, and Homer Simpson works at a nuclear power plant.

lines.GREECE: Homer is the ancient Greek poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey.
lines.PLANT: Homer Simpson works at the Springfield nuclear power plant.

hints.explanation: Hatmakers once used mercury to make felt, and mercury poisoning is often linked to the phrase "mad as a hatter".

lines.HAT: The Mad Hatter is Wonderland's famous hat-wearer.
lines.MERCURY: Mercury used in making felt hats poisoned some hatters.

hints.explanation: The Toronto Maple Leafs are a hockey team.

lines.HOCKEY: The Maple Leafs are one of the NHL's oldest teams.
lines.LEAF: Toronto's NHL team is the Maple Leafs.

hints.explanation: Iron Maiden is a heavy metal band.

lines.IRON: Iron is the first word of the band name Iron Maiden.
lines.METAL: Iron Maiden is one of the best-known heavy metal bands.

hints.explanation: Elvis Presley is called the King of Rock and Roll.

lines.ROLL: Elvis was a rock and roll pioneer.

hints.explanation: The saying goes that lightning never strikes twice.

lines.LIGHTNING: Lightning is said never to strike twice in the same place.
lines.STRIKE: The saying says lightning never strikes the same place twice.

hints.explanation: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, the March Hare hosts the mad tea party with the Hatter.

lines.MARCH: The March Hare is one of Wonderland's oddest characters.
lines.TEA: Alice joins a mad tea party in Wonderland.

hints.explanation: Finding Nemo has seagulls shouting Mine and Bruce the shark.

lines.MINE: The seagulls in Finding Nemo shout Mine! Mine!
lines.SHARK: Bruce the shark in Finding Nemo says fish are friends, not food.

hints.explanation: James Bond, the famous spy, orders martinis, which are often garnished with an olive.

lines.OLIVE: A martini is often served with an olive.
lines.SPY: Spy James Bond likes his martini shaken, not stirred.

hints.explanation: There are poison dart frogs, and in fairy tales a frog turns into a prince.

lines.POISON: Poison dart frogs are brightly colored and toxic.
lines.PRINCE: In The Frog Prince, a spell is broken and a frog becomes a prince.

hints.explanation: A vinyl record spins on a turntable, and a top spins on its point.

lines.RECORD: A record spins on the turntable while it plays.
lines.TOP: A spinning top twirls on its point until it slows and topples.

hints.explanation: WALL-E is Pixar's little robot who compacts trash on an abandoned Earth.

lines.TRASH: WALL-E spends his days stacking cubes of trash.

hints.explanation: A sports team plays in a league, and Jules Verne wrote 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea.

lines.SEA: Jules Verne wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
lines.SPORT: Many sports are organized into leagues.

hints.explanation: Silver is the medal for second place, and a second is a unit of time.

lines.SILVER: A silver medal goes to second place.
lines.TIME: A second is a small unit of time.

hints.explanation: The Rolling Stones' logo is a tongue sticking out, and some people can roll their tongue.

lines.STONE: "A rolling stone gathers no moss," and the band took the name.
lines.TONGUE: The Rolling Stones' logo is lips with a tongue out, and tongue rolling is a trick some people can do.
